record.paper_title: Quantum Information Theory: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Additivity of classical channel capacity quantity
record.original_question: Let a memoryless quantum channel N have classical one-use quantity χ_max(N), defined as the maximum, over all ensembles of input states, of the Holevo quantity for the corresponding channel outputs. Is χ_max additive for all pairs of quantum channels, meaning χ_max(N1 ⊗ N2) = χ_max(N1) + χ_max(N2)? Equivalently, can entangling inputs across separate channel uses ever increase the achievable classical communication rate beyond what is obtained by optimizing one use at a time?

evidence.quote: We do not know whether this is the capacity of a quantum channel; if the use of entanglement between separate inputs to the channel helps to increase channel capacity, it might be possible to exceed this χmax(N).
This can be addressed by answering a question that is simple to state: Is χmax(N) additive [1]?
That is, if we have two quantum channels N1 and N2, is χmax(N1 ⊗ N2)=χmax(N1)+χmax(N2).
The question is whether strictly more capacity can be attained by using the tensor product of two channels jointly than by using them separately.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A, \mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and let $\mathcal{N}: \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a quantum channel (a completely positive, trace-preserving linear map). For a finite ensemble $\mathcal{E} = \{p_i, \rho_i\}$ of probability weights $p_i \geq 0$, $\sum_i p_i = 1$, and density operators $\rho_i$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$, define the Holevo quantity of the output ensemble as
$$\chi(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{N}) = S\!\left(\sum_i p_i \mathcal{N}(\rho_i)\right) - \sum_i p_i\, S(\mathcal{N}(\rho_i)),$$
where $S(\sigma) = -\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma \log \sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy. Define the one-shot classical (Holevo) capacity
$$\chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}) = \sup_{\mathcal{E}} \chi(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{N}).$$
For any two quantum channels $\mathcal{N}_1, \mathcal{N}_2$, one has the trivial inequality $\chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1 \otimes \mathcal{N}_2) \geq \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1) + \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_2)$.

Question: Does equality
$$\chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1 \otimes \mathcal{N}_2) = \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1) + \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_2)$$
hold for every pair of quantum channels $\mathcal{N}_1, \mathcal{N}_2$? Equivalently, can the use of entangled input states across two channel uses ever strictly increase the Holevo quantity beyond the sum of single-channel optima?
artifact.status_search_result: The additivity of the Holevo capacity $\chi_{\max}$ was disproved by M. B. Hastings in 2009, who exhibited (via a random-unitary construction) pairs of channels for which $\chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1 \otimes \mathcal{N}_2) > \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_1) + \chi_{\max}(\mathcal{N}_2)$. This resolved the long-standing additivity conjecture (equivalent to additivity of minimum output entropy as shown by Shor) in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Superadditivity of communication capacity using entangled inputs
status_evidence.snippet: Hastings (2009) shows there exist channels with χ_max(N⊗N) > 2 χ_max(N), disproving the additivity conjecture for Holevo capacity.
status_evidence.claim: Additivity of χ_max is false in general.
